test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 18 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: A man buys 10 identical articles for a total of ₹15. If he sells each of them for ₹1.7, then his profit percentage will be _______%(rounded off to two decimal place).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of 1 article = 15 ÷ 10 = &rupee;1.5

Selling Price (SP) of 1 article = &rupee;1.7

Profit = 1.7 − 1.5 = &rupee;0.2

Profit % = (0.2 ÷ 1.5) × 100 = 13.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8de887482f38f1d3b080ead975e4e01b417ab2d9c08a239858ac82a7ba7e44c9.png] 

**Given:**

Total Cost Price (CP) of 10 articles = &rupee;15

Selling Price (SP) of 1 article = &rupee;1.7

**Formula Used:**

Total SP = SP of 1 article × Total articles

Profit = Total SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total SP of 10 articles = 1.7 × 10 = &rupee;17

⇒ Total CP of 10 articles = &rupee;15

⇒ Profit = 17 − 15 = &rupee;2

⇒ Profit % = (2 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 200 ÷ 15 = 13.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Cost Price is greater than Selling Price, a loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Percentage Change

If there are successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by: a + b + (a × b ÷ 100).
